logs:
2026-06-18T02:17:03Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-k4mnr ERROR db.pool - timeout acquiring connection after 30000ms
2026-06-18T02:17:10Z pgbouncer-7f6c89c6d8-v7qmt LOG pool=payments cl_active=198 cl_waiting=101 sv_active=64
2026-06-18T02:17:18Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-k4mnr ERROR sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit reached, connection acquisition timed out

root_cause: The nightly batch consumed the available pgbouncer server connections and left interactive services without enough database capacity.

actions.step: Scale payments-api replicas to spread the incoming request load.
Raise PostgreSQL max_connections while the batch workload is still running.
Pause the nightly batch and restart pgbouncer to clear the saturated pool.

postmortem: The scheduled batch consumed the shared database pool and caused interactive requests to exceed their connection wait limits. Scaling application pods did not create additional database capacity, while pausing the batch and restarting pgbouncer restored service.

alert: Postgres data volume critically full due to retained WAL
logs:
2026-06-29T03:54:03Z postgres-primary-0 postgres[2641] WARNING disk usage on /var/lib/postgresql/data reached 99%
2026-06-29T03:54:10Z postgres-primary-0 postgres[2641] ERROR could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.2641": No space left on device

2026-06-29T03:54:26Z ledger-service-6d8f7c9b5-r4mkt ERROR pq: could not extend file: No space left on device
2026-06-29T03:54:43Z postgres-primary-0 postgres[2641] WARNING checkpoint failed because filesystem is full
root_cause: A retired replication slot continued retaining WAL and consumed nearly all free PostgreSQL storage.

actions.step: Remove old PostgreSQL and application logs to reclaim filesystem space.
Drop the abandoned replication slot after confirming it was no longer required.
Expand the PostgreSQL PVC to add additional storage headroom.

postmortem: An obsolete replication slot retained hundreds of gigabytes of WAL and filled the database volume. Dropping the slot released the retained WAL, and expanding the PVC provided additional protection against another immediate capacity event.
